---
title: "Who Receives Technical Violations?"
format: html
---

**Who receives technical violations?**

1. What proportion of youth on probation supervision receive a technical violation during a probation term? How does this vary across race/ethnicity, sex, age, and risk level? 

2. What proportion of violations filed by a PO are rejected by supervisor or prosecutor?

```{r include=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
###############################
### import dallas analytic file
###############################

### set sharepoint path using sp_data_path and file.path function 
sharepoint_jj_av_dallas_analytic_data <- file.path(sp_data_path,"Data/analysis")

df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file <- read_delim(file.path(sharepoint_jj_av_dallas_analytic_data,
                      "df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file.txt"),
                      delim = "|") %>% 
  mutate(offense_referral_risk_level = 
           case_when(
             offense_referral_risk_level=="Low Risk" ~ 1,
             offense_referral_risk_level%in%c("Medium-Low Risk",
                             "Medium-High Risk",
                             "Moderate Risk") ~ 2,
             offense_referral_risk_level=="High Risk" ~ 3,             
             offense_referral_risk_level%in%c("Unknown/Not Administered") ~ 4,
             TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
         ### use factor function to assign labels to values
         offense_referral_risk_level = factor(offense_referral_risk_level,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels =  c("Low Risk", 
                     "Moderate Risk", 
                     "High Risk",
                     "Unknown/Not Administered")),
         offense_referral_needs_level = 
           case_when(
             offense_referral_needs_level=="Low Needs" ~ 1,
             offense_referral_needs_level=="Moderate Needs" ~ 2,
             offense_referral_needs_level=="High Needs" ~ 3,             
             offense_referral_needs_level%in%c("Unknown/Not Administered") ~ 4,
             TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
         ### use factor function to assign labels to values
         offense_referral_needs_level = factor(offense_referral_needs_level,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels = c("Low Needs", 
                    "Moderate Needs", 
                    "High Needs",
                    "Unknown/Not Administered"))) |> 
  ### remove FY 2023 Completion (year is incomplete based on timing of data pull) 
  filter(supervision_end_fy!=2023)

```

# 1. Technical Violations Overview

**NOTE:** All analysis of technical violations in this section (e.g., supervision episodes with at least one technical violation) refers to the filing of any technical violations regardless of outcome/disposition. 

<br>

## Table 1. By FY: Percentage of Supervision Episodes/Referrals with a Technical Violation

```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### create denominator -- unique referrals for entire sample
unique_referrals_sample_denom <- n_distinct(df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file$unique_id,
                                            df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file$referral_number)

### create denominator -- unique supervision episodes
unique_supervision_episode_denom <- n_distinct(df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file$unique_supervision_id)

### create denominator -- unique youth for entire sample
unique_youth_sample_denom <- n_distinct(df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file$unique_id)

### unique youth and referrals per FY
df_technical_violations_per_year <- df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(supervision_end_fy) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(`Unique Youth (N)` = n_distinct(unique_id),
            `Unique Referrals (N)` = n_distinct(unique_referral_id),
            `Unique Supervision Episodes (N)` = n_distinct(unique_supervision_id),
            `Supervision Episodes, Percent of Sample (column %)` = scales::percent(`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`/unique_supervision_episode_denom,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`FY of Completion` = supervision_end_fy) %>% 
  mutate(`FY of Completion` = as.character(`FY of Completion`))

### overall
df_technical_violations_overall <- df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(`Unique Youth (N)` = n_distinct(unique_id),
            `Unique Referrals (N)` = n_distinct(unique_referral_id),
            `Unique Supervision Episodes (N)` = n_distinct(unique_supervision_id),
            `Supervision Episodes, Percent of Sample (column %)` = scales::percent(`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`/unique_supervision_episode_denom,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1)) %>% 
  mutate(`FY of Completion` = "Overall")

### combine tables for kable
df_technical_violations_per_year_table <- rbind(df_technical_violations_per_year,df_technical_violations_overall)

### print table via kableextra
kable(df_technical_violations_per_year_table, 
      format.args = list(big.mark = ","), 
      align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", 
                                       "hover", 
                                       "condensed", 
                                       "responsive"), 
                 row_label_position = "l") %>% 
  row_spec(6, bold = TRUE)
```

<br>

## Table 2. By Race/Ethnicity: Percentage of Supervision Episodes/Referrals with a Technical Violation

```{r echo=FALSE,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
### unique youth, referrals, and supervision episodes
df_technical_violations_race <- df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(race_clean) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(`Unique Youth (N)` = n_distinct(unique_id),
            `Unique Referrals (N)` = n_distinct(unique_referral_id),
            `Unique Supervision Episodes (N)` = n_distinct(unique_supervision_id),
            `Supervision Episodes, Percent of Sample (column %)` = scales::percent(`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`/unique_supervision_episode_denom,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (RRI to White youth)` = round((n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`)/0.1184573, digits = 1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (RRI to White youth)` = round((n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`)/0.0261708,digits = 1)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::rename(`Race/Ethnicity` = race_clean)

### overall
df_technical_violations_overall <- df_dallas_county_av_supervision_analytic_file %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(`Unique Youth (N)` = n_distinct(unique_id),
            `Unique Referrals (N)` = n_distinct(unique_referral_id),
            `Unique Supervision Episodes (N)` = n_distinct(unique_supervision_id),
            `Supervision Episodes, Percent of Sample (column %)` = scales::percent(`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`/unique_supervision_episode_denom,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[technical_violation_flag==1])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one technical violations (RRI to White youth)` = NA,
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (row %)` = scales::percent(n_distinct(unique_supervision_id[new_offense_violation_count>0 & !is.na(new_offense_violation_count)])/`Unique Supervision Episodes (N)`,
                                                                       accuracy = .1),
            `Supervision Episodes, with at least one new offense violation (RRI to White youth)` = NA) %>% 
  mutate(`Race/Ethnicity` = "Overall")

### combine tables for kable
df_technical_violations_race_table <- rbind(df_technical_violations_race,df_technical_violations_overall)

### print table via kableextra

      format.args = list(big.mark = ","), 
      align=rep('c')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped",

                                       "responsive"),
```

# 3. Supervisor/Prosecutor Rejections 

**Business Rule:** According to Dallas County, all of the technical violation records without a referral number indicate that a PO filed the violation, but that it was rejected by a supervisor.

**NOTE:** Only about 2% of all violations fit this criteria -- not sure if it warrants analysis (especially anything disaggregated). The Dallas team mentioned several factors to consider regarding rejections in general as well as the small percentage of violations that appear in our sample. A fair amount of informal rejection is possible (possible violations are rejected/not approved before any data would be entered or a violation would actually be filed). PO has to get permission from supervisor before filing a violation so there should be very few rejected violations (i.e., PO's will likely only formally file a violation if they feel confident it will be approved by a supervisor).Thus, 2% really only reflects what is in the data system but likely does not speak to the real trend.

<br><br>
